newsitem.title: LIBERIA: Taiwan gives Liberia $1 million for elections.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan gives Liberia $1 million for elections.

text.p: Taiwan has donated one million dollars to help organise elections in war-ravaged Liberia where arch rival China also has a diplomatic mission.
"This cheque will go a long way in helping with the work of the independent elections commission," said Nigerian Foreign Minister Tom Ikimi on Thursday as he received the money.
Ikimi represented the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) which brokered a peace plan last year under which elections are scheduled for this month.
Charles Taylor, who launched the war which has killed at least 150,000 people since 1989, said he had personally negotiated the assistance from Taiwan during a visit in February.
Africa is a battleground for the diplomatic war for recognition between China and Taiwan. China has viewed Taiwan as a rebel-held province since it split away in 1949 during civil war.
Taiwan on Tuesday scored a small victory when it won recognition from Sao Tome and Principe, a tiny former Portuguese island clolony off the West African coast.
Liberia's elections are pencilled in for May 30, but election officials are discussing a possible delay with ECOWAS leaders.
Only Taylor favours keeping the May election date, but on Thursday suggested he would accept a postponement if necessary.
"The National Patriotic Party will cooperate, will accept and abide by any action taken by ECOWAS along the lines of helping resolve the Liberian crisis," Taylor told reporters.
Liberia was founded by freed American slaves in 1847.
